subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Les Deux Magots and Existentialism
description: A short lesson to help you apply Les Deux Magots and Existentialism.

hook.text: Jean-Paul Sartre and Simone de Beauvoir wrote existentialist philosophy at Les Deux Magots in Saint-Germain-des-Prés.

buildup.text: During World War II, the café served as their office. They couldn't afford to heat their apartments, so they wrote here.

discovery.text: Sartre wrote much of 'Being and Nothingness' at these tables. De Beauvoir composed 'The Second Sex' nearby at Café de Flore.

twist.text: The café became so associated with intellectualism that tourists replaced thinkers. Sartre himself eventually left.

climax.text: Les Deux Magots awards an annual literary prize. The café's intellectual legacy continues even as its clientele changed.

punchline.text: Existentialism was written in a café because the heat was free.

quiz.question: Why did Sartre and de Beauvoir write at Les Deux Magots?
options: They couldn't afford to heat their apartments and used the café as an office
It was required by their publisher

details.summary: Les Deux Magots, directly across from Cafe de Flore in Saint-Germain, was another intellectual landmark. Hemingway, James Joyce, and later the existentialists all worked there. It awards an annual literary prize. The friendly rivalry with Flore defined the creative energy of the neighborhood.
details.whyItMatters: Les Deux Magots shows how cafes clustered together can create an intellectual ecosystem where competition and proximity amplify creative output.
takeaways: Les Deux Magots sits across from Cafe de Flore in Saint-Germain
Hemingway, Joyce, and Sartre all frequented it
It awards an annual literary prize to emerging writers

faq.question: What is the Les Deux Magots literary prize?
faq.answer: Established in 1933, it is an annual award for a French novel or collection that displays originality and independence from commercial literary trends. Past winners include Raymond Queneau. The prize maintains the cafe's connection to literary culture.

faq.question: How did Saint-Germain become the intellectual center of Paris?
faq.answer: The neighborhood's proximity to the Sorbonne, publishing houses, and affordable housing drew writers and thinkers. Cafes served as their offices and salons. The concentration of creative people in a small area around Flore and Les Deux Magots created a self-reinforcing intellectual community.
